images.title: Fixing a total to fix the mean
images.purpose: Shows the three steps that correct the coconut harvest mean: total, corrected total, corrected mean.
images.composition: Three large rounded boxes in one row across the middle of the frame, joined by two right pointing arrows, each box with a short caption above it. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Three equal rounded rectangles in a single row, evenly spaced, with thin dark outlines. Box 1 has a teal (#0072B2) border and holds '25.6 × 15 = 384'; its caption above is 'total'. Box 2 has a vermilion (#D55E00) border and holds '384 − 3 = 381'; its caption above is 'remove the extra 3'. Box 3 has a reddish purple (#CC79A7) border, slightly thicker, and holds '381 ÷ 15 = 25.4'; its caption above is 'correct mean'. Two grey arrows point right, one from box 1 to box 2 and one from box 2 to box 3. Exactly 3 boxes, 2 arrows, 6 pieces of text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Mean times count gives the total, so fixing the total fixes the mean.
images.description: Shows the three steps that correct the coconut harvest mean: total, corrected total, corrected mean.
images.context: 15 trees, noted mean 25.6, one count 3 too high; corrected mean 25.4 (a drop of 3 shared over 15).

image_decisions.why: The concept is a three step chain; seeing the chain in one row makes the method clear without the data list.
